drug_class: Monoclonal antibody; sclerostin inhibitor; bone-forming agent

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin A (>10,000 IU/day)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Excessive vitamin A antagonizes Wnt signaling and may reduce romosozumab efficacy in bone formation
avoid_supplements.action: Limit vitamin A supplementation to recommended dietary allowance (700-900 mcg/day); monitor intake from multivitamins and retinoid products

avoid_supplements.name: Systemic corticosteroid supplements (if used concurrently with oral corticosteroids)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Corticosteroids inhibit bone formation and directly antagonize romosozumab's mechanism; significantly reduce therapeutic benefit
avoid_supplements.action: Use lowest effective corticosteroid dose; coordinate with prescriber; consider alternative therapies

caution_supplements.name: Calcium supplements (>1,200 mg/day total intake)
caution_supplements.mechanism: While calcium is essential for bone health, excessive supplementation may cause hypercalcemia when combined with romosozumab's bone-forming effects
caution_supplements.action: Maintain calcium intake of 1,000-1,200 mg/day from diet and supplements combined; monitor serum calcium periodically

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin D3 supplementation
caution_supplements.mechanism: Vitamin D is necessary for calcium absorption and bone metabolism; deficiency may reduce romosozumab efficacy, but excess may increase hypercalcemia risk
caution_supplements.action: Ensure adequate vitamin D status (25-75 ng/mL); supplement if deficient; typical dose 1,000-2,000 IU/day

caution_supplements.name: Phosphorus supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Phosphorus imbalance may affect calcium-phosphate homeostasis and bone mineralization during romosozumab therapy
caution_supplements.action: Maintain adequate dietary phosphorus; avoid excessive supplementation; monitor serum phosphorus if symptomatic

avoid_foods.name: Excessive sodium intake (>2,300 mg/day)
avoid_foods.mechanism: High sodium increases urinary calcium excretion, potentially reducing bone mineral density gains achieved by romosozumab
avoid_foods.action: Limit dietary sodium to <2,300 mg/day; reduce processed and cured foods

caution_foods.name: Calcium-rich foods (dairy, leafy greens, fortified products)
caution_foods.mechanism: Dietary calcium is essential for bone metabolism and romosozumab efficacy; inadequate intake reduces therapeutic benefit
caution_foods.action: Consume 3-4 servings of calcium-rich foods daily to achieve 1,000-1,200 mg/day total calcium intake

caution_foods.name: Vitamin D-containing foods (fatty fish, egg yolks, fortified milk)
caution_foods.mechanism: Dietary vitamin D supports calcium absorption and bone health; deficiency may impair romosozumab response
caution_foods.action: Include vitamin D-rich foods in diet 2-3 times weekly; obtain 10-30 minutes sunlight exposure daily when possible

caution_foods.name: Caffeine (>400 mg/day)
caution_foods.mechanism: Excessive caffeine may increase urinary calcium loss and slightly reduce bone mineral density; moderate intake is safe
caution_foods.action: Limit caffeine from coffee, tea, and soft drinks to <400 mg/day (approximately 3-4 cups coffee); compensate with adequate calcium intake

monitoring_notes: Romosozumab is a monoclonal antibody with no hepatic metabolism, minimizing traditional drug-supplement interactions. Monitor serum calcium, phosphorus, and magnesium periodically, as romosozumab increases bone turnover and may affect mineral homeostasis. Assess vitamin D status at baseline and annually; maintain adequate calcium intake to optimize bone formation efficacy.
